candidates.changed_node: $close / (TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8) as a multiplicative headroom normaliser on the momentum fragment
candidates.rationale: Scales 10-day mean-return momentum by the close-to-21-day-high ratio: momentum is trusted more when the stock still has headroom below its own ceiling, and discounted once it is already pressing against the high. P1's momentum term carries no sense of range position; P2's range position carries no directional content. The ratio is the missing normaliser each parent lacks alone.

candidates.changed_node: TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) used as a multiplicative confidence weight on the low-anchored price ratio
candidates.rationale: Weights the close-vs-21-day-low ratio by 21-day dollar volume: a bounce off the low is more likely genuine, information-driven demand when it trades with real liquidity, and more likely noise in a thin name. P2 has no liquidity context; P3 has no price-action content. The product is a liquidity-confirmed support signal.

candidates.changed_node: $high - $low normalised by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) + 1e-8, replacing P4's ranked distance-from-high numerator
candidates.rationale: Normalises the day's high-low range by 21-day dollar-volume liquidity: the same nominal range reflects real price discovery in a liquid name and is more likely a stale-quote artefact in a thin one. This generalises P4's 'scale a price-structure signal by liquidity' pattern to a two-sided range, using P3's raw liquidity level instead of a liquidity rank.

candidates.changed_node: $earnings_per_share * TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) as a liquidity-weighted earnings numerator
candidates.rationale: Weights earnings-per-share by its own 21-day dollar volume before scaling by price: a cheap, high-liquidity earner is a tradeable mispricing, while the same EPS in an illiquid name is a value trap that cannot be arbitraged efficiently. P3's liquidity level carries no value content on its own; P1's earnings-yield ratio carries no liquidity conditioning.

Ranks a momentum-minus-earnings 'over-extension' term, then divides by a rank of distance from the 21-day high: the same over-extension score is weighted far more for a name still well below its own ceiling than for one already near it. Reuses P4's rank-normalisation pattern but applies it to a fresh numerator that blends P1's two fields by subtraction instead of ranking them separately.

candidates.changed_node: TS_RANK(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21), 60), a liquidity-surge-vs-own-history multiplier on momentum
candidates.rationale: Multiplies 10-day momentum by a time-series rank of current liquidity against its own trailing 60 days: momentum is weighted up only where a name's OWN liquidity has recently surged relative to its own history. That is a self-referential attention filter, distinct from P4's cross-sectional liquidity rank and from P1's unconditioned momentum term. A genuinely different mechanism from the pair-5 child on the same two parents.

candidates.changed_node: multiplicative combination of TS_MEAN($return, 10) and TS_DELTA($close, 2), a short-vs-medium horizon agreement term
candidates.rationale: Multiplies 10-day mean return by the raw 2-day price change: rewards names where the latest 2-day move agrees in direction with the medium-term drift (confirmed, accelerating momentum) and dampens or flips the score when the last two days already contradict the 10-day trend. P1 has no short-horizon check on its momentum term; P5's 2-day signal (sign times a volume-surge rank) carries no medium-term context at all.

candidates.changed_node: $earnings_per_share / (TS_MIN($low, 21) + 1e-8), a low-anchored value term, contrasted with TS_MEAN($return, 10)
candidates.rationale: Anchors earnings yield to the 21-day low instead of the current close, so a name that has merely fallen hard doesn't mechanically show an inflated yield, then subtracts raw 10-day momentum. This ranks names that are still cheap relative to their own floor and have not yet rallied highest, separating unrecognised value from value the market has already started re-rating. Distinct mechanism from the pair-1 child: here P2's range fragment reshapes the value normaliser itself, rather than scaling the momentum term.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
